title: Measurement record v2: the authored half of catalog/record.json, with performance as data
description: One per measurements/<dir>/. TOML so stdlib tomllib reads it (CI is stdlib-only, python 3.12). Carries ONLY what no artifact already says. Everything derivable (owner recipe, tool, version, pins, verified dates, spec resources/lifecycle, staging, chip/arch/vendor from the instance name, threads_per_core and OpenBLAS corename from a host file, reverse cross-code links, overall status) is computed by gen_catalog.py and must NOT be authored here. v2 adds performance fields to the SAME record: no second file. New fields are optional except where a v1 field was ambiguous (billed_basis on any row with billed_s or overhead_s). Every derived quantity (vcpus, physical cores, utilisation ratios, binding resource, effective $/hr, $/result from throughput, series curves, cost knee, n and spread per configuration, pipeline totals) is computed by gen_catalog.py and must NOT be authored. So is the GPU utilisation plateau (from gpu.util_series).

schema.description: 1 = not yet migrated (warns); 2 = performance fields reviewed. Additive optional fields never bump this; a rename or a change of meaning does.

result_unit.description: The denominator of every $/result in this record, in words. Required because the arithmetic identity cannot be checked without it (abundance-real's billed $/result is per sample of two).

results_per_run.description: How many result_units one run row produces. compute_usd == wall_s * usd_hr / 3600 / results_per_run.

workload.description: What one result computed, as numbers a consumer can MATCH against (never extrapolate from). Defaults every run's size.

size.description: Named magnitudes of one result's input/work. Prefer the common keys: reads, read_pairs, bases, atoms, steps, simulated_ns, basis_functions, kpoints, events, samples, files, cells, voxels, sequences, families, generations. A key is a claim: it must be printed in the README.

input_gib.description: Bytes staged in for one run (GiB). Printed in the README.

note.description: Shape in words (shared index, per-sample fan-out, serial phase ...). Prose, not parsed.

throughput_unit.description: Unit of every run's `throughput`, e.g. 'ns/day', 'reads/s', 'events/s'. The denominator is one of s|min|hr|day so gen_catalog can convert without a units library. Only where a rate is the tool's natural unit (MD ns/day, per-read aligners); a forced rate is a second result unit.

throughput_is_result.description: true when the numerator of throughput_unit IS result_unit (GROMACS: result = 1 ns, throughput in ns/day). Then compute_usd == usd_hr / throughput_per_hour is checked, and $/result is derived for rows that print none.

timing.description: Record-wide definitions of the time fields, overridable per run. Required in v2 whenever a row carries billed_s/overhead_s: v1's billed_s meant three different windows in different records.

wall.description: What wall_s times, in words: 'bwa's own Real time', 'mdrun only', 'the task command, timed in-script'.

billed_basis.description: spawn-task = the completion record's started_at -> ended_at (wrapper start to stage-out done); ec2 = CloudTrail RunInstances -> TerminateInstances (adds boot and shutdown); spawn-task-minus-baseline = spawn-task minus a measured no-tool copy (lith-vs-copy-real); sum-of-tasks = derived for a pipeline from its task rows; authored only on an aggregate row whose README billed is the sum of its tasks' windows (the header comment says which windows). unavailable = the README prints a billed figure but no completion record survives, so billed_s/billed_usd stay absent; shared-window = one billed window covers this row and others (two walls in one task, five aligns on one box), so no per-row billed figure exists; unattributed = the README prints this billed window but neither a surviving completion record nor CloudTrail reproduces it (warns: a README number nobody can source). spawn-task-partial = from spawn's started_at to a marker inside the task that the README names (cromwell-wdl-real: to the end of the workflow run, before the cross-check), a sub-window of the completion record. ec2-to-spawn-end = CloudTrail RunInstances -> spawn's ended_at (pyscf-real: 'instance launch to stage-out'). spawn-task-minus-baseline also covers a spawn window minus a measured interval the README names (squidpy-real: a replicate pass).

id.description: Durable identifier: accession, DOI, release+path, RODA bucket key.

pins.description: Path (repo-relative or relative to this dir) to a sha256 manifest that pins it. The record never copies a hash.

unpinned.description: Why there is no pin. Mutually exclusive with pins; surfaces as a gap in record.json.

from_recipe.description: When the bytes are another recipe's run output or staged prefix (tier run-output / shared stage).

items.description: A $ figure needs the time and rate it was computed from (check_pages enforces it): compute_usd needs wall_s and usd_hr, billed_usd needs billed_s (or wall_s + overhead_s) and usd_hr. A run the README prices nowhere carries no usd_hr and no $.

instance.description: EC2 instance type. '<family>.unrecorded' when an artifact names the family but not the size (vCPUs are then not derived): never a guessed size.

purpose.description: diagnostic rows (gw-real's arms, probes, superseded runs) never feed a 'which box' answer. control = a baseline arm measured for comparison and comparable to the primary rows (lith-vs-copy-real's 'today'), not a probe. Pipeline per-task rows take the purpose of the result they belong to, not diagnostic.

image.description: 'recipe' = the owner recipe's pin for this run's arch (resolved and compared at generation time); otherwise a full @sha256 reference, or 'unrecorded' when no artifact names the image (absent would claim the recipe's pin).

date.description: Run date from the completion record. Backfill may use the git date results/ was added, flagged date_source = 'git'.

threads_per_core.description: Author ONLY when no host file exists; otherwise read from host.

host.description: Path to this run's host-facts file (host.txt etc.); threads_per_core, cpu model/part and openblas corename are read from it.

wall_s.description: Tool wall, the README table's wall column.

overhead_s.description: When the table gives overhead instead of billed: billed_s = wall_s + overhead_s.

usd_hr.description: On-demand price the run was costed at (spawn-printed, region below). A historical fact, not a current price.

peak_kind.description: rss = the tool's RSS; cgroup-memory.peak = whole-run kernel peak (counts page cache); cgroup-memory.current-max = 1 Hz max of memory.current; cgroup-anon-max = 1 Hz max of memory.stat anon (the OOM floor); host-used = MemTotal - MemAvailable (counts the tmpfs). Different kinds are not comparable; a consumer sizing RAM wants anon or rss.

results.description: Path to the run's committed result artifact(s).

id.description: Unique within the record. Needed only when something references the row (superseded_by, a series that selects by id).

in.description: Series ids this row belongs to. One row may sit in several (bwa's c8g.4xlarge is the 16-core rung of the knee AND Graviton4 in the generation ladder).

task.description: Pipeline task name (spec basename). Rows sharing `attempt` and differing in `task` are one end-to-end result; gen_catalog sums their windows and $ into results[] -- the aggregate is never authored a second time.

attempt.description: Groups the tasks of one end-to-end result, and separates repeats of one configuration (r1, r2, w1).

variant.description: Whatever differs between otherwise-identical rows and has no field ('awk counter on the timed path', 'ALT-aware 01-align'). Part of the configuration key that n and spread are derived over.

superseded_by.description: id of the row that replaces this one. A superseded row is kept (it is spread evidence) but never answers a query.

run_outcome.description: Whether the RUN finished, distinct from whether its checks held. failed rungs are what a 'wall' verdict rests on (GPAW at 64 ranks); no-capacity records an acquisition that never placed (dated, region-scoped).

ranks.description: MPI ranks (1 for a non-MPI tool).

threads_per_rank.description: OpenMP / tool threads per rank. workers == ranks x threads_per_rank x concurrent is checked.

concurrent.description: Independent jobs sharing the box (layout packing, MPS clients). throughput is then the AGGREGATE; per-job is derived.

bind.description: Launch binding as run ('--map-by slot:PE=4 --bind-to core', 'none'). The 7x GROMACS lever; free text because launchers differ.

size.description: Overrides workload.size for this row (size sweeps).

throughput.description: In the record's throughput_unit, as the tool or the script reports it. Aggregate over `concurrent` jobs.

ec2_s.description: RunInstances -> TerminateInstances from CloudTrail, when retrieved (plink2-real/results/billed-windows.txt). The launch-to-terminate window a bill is actually made of.

phase_s.description: Where the non-tool time went, from spawn's command.log phase stamps (spawn >= 0.104.0) or lagotto history. Each is a measured interval, not a remainder. tool == wall_s when both present.

acquire.description: Capacity wait before the instance existed (lagotto history WAIT). Unbilled, but time-to-answer.

setup.description: In-task time before useful work that is not staging: CUDA PTX JIT, index load, JVM warmup.

source.description: Path to the file the phases were read from.

avg_cores.description: cgroup cpu.stat usage_usec delta / wall_s delta over the tool window. Cores-equivalent busy; on an SMT box it counts hardware threads.

peak_cores.description: Max 1 Hz delta of usage_usec (measurements/sizing-ratio instrument). Separates 'never parallelises past N' from 'N-way phase then serial'.

anon_gib.description: Max memory.stat anon when peak_kind is something else (bwa-real cross-chip rows carry both).

tmpfs_peak_gib.description: High-water mark of host /tmp (df), the staging space = 1/2 instance RAM on the spawn task path. Picks the family as often as RSS does (fastp, kraken2).

staged_gib.description: Bytes this row staged in, when it differs from workload.input_gib.

data_path.description: How inputs reached the tool. stage-default = spawn's stage-in at the AWS CLI default (10 requests, 8 MiB parts) -- its meaning is tied to spawn_version (spawn#1256 would change it); stage-crt = the CRT transfer client, peak-NIC target, 16 MiB parts. instance-store-copy = copied to the instance's local NVMe before the tool reads it.

request_usd.description: S3 GET/HEAD/LIST charges at list price as if you own the bucket (Payer: BucketOwner). Not in billed_usd; total is derived.

price_source.description: Where usd_hr came from. 'spawn' = the hourly spawn printed at launch; 'truffle' / 'pricing-api' = looked up for the run's date; 'rate-card' = a published list rate the README quotes, which no run artifact records. A historical fact: never a current price.

simd_path.description: The SIMD/kernel path the TOOL reports it took (GROMACS 'ARM_NEON_ASIMD', bowtie2's x86-64-v3 fallback warning, bwa-mem2 'avx512bw'). Authored from the tool's log; never inferred from the chip.

build.description: Build channel when image_resolved does not say it (licensed source build, NGC, DLAMI-native).

launch.description: task = spawn task run (container, TaskSpec); launch = spawn launch --ami ... --command (raw instance; the GPU path until spawn#601).

ami.description: AMI id and name, for launch rows (the DLAMI).

gpu.description: Present iff the row used an accelerator. The card view; the row's avg_cores / peak_gib stay the system view, so a GPU row shows all four rented resources. The utilisation summary is derived from util_series (see there); the plateau is never authored.

count.description: Devices the tool USED (not the instance's count; that is truffle's).

mem_mib.description: Per-device memory.total in MiB, as nvidia-smi prints it. Instrument units, so the value round-trips against the committed CSV without a conversion.

cuda.description: CUDA runtime the binary ran against (not the AMI's default toolkit; Amber 26 needs < 12.9 where the DLAMI's default is 13.2).

runtime.description: native = on the DLAMI host; docker-privileged = the --privileged --gpus all form that survives the cgroup v2 device reset.

offload.description: Which parts ran on the GPU, in the tool's own terms ('nonbonded', 'pme', 'update').

offload_evidence.description: The tool's own log line(s) proving offload ('1 GPU selected', 'PME tasks will do all aspects on the GPU'). Required unless offload_evidence_absent says why it is not: card presence is not GPU use.

util_series.description: Path to the committed 1 Hz nvidia-smi / DCGM CSV (a utilization.gpu column, % values; a memory.used column in MiB if present). gen_catalog derives util_plateau_pct (median over the active window: first to last sample >= 50% of the series max), util_mean_pct, util_peak_pct, active_fraction and, when memory.used is present, hbm_peak_mib. None of those is authored.

hbm_peak_mib.description: Max memory.used (MiB), summed over the devices used. Author it only when no util_series carries memory.used.

mps_clients.description: NVIDIA MPS clients sharing each device (== concurrent when packing one card).

offload_evidence_absent.description: Why no log line is quoted (only the launch flags survive). The offload is then ASSERTED FROM FLAGS, not proven by a log: gen_catalog derives offload_basis = 'flags' (else 'log'). One of this or offload_evidence is required.

series.description: A sweep: rows that differ on ONE axis and are held equal on everything else. The curve (speedup, efficiency, marginal gain per doubling, $/result per rung, cost knee) is DERIVED from the member rows; only the axis, the held set, the equal-work proof and the author's reading are authored.

id.description: Run rows join a series with in = [id].

axis.description: The ONE thing varied. 'size' means workload size (run.size); 'layout' means ranks x threads at fixed workers; 'offload' = which stages run on the GPU; 'accelerator' = CPU vs GPU boxes for one result; 'instance' is a free comparison and gets no derived curve.

size_key.description: For axis = size: which run.size key is the abscissa.

held.description: What is equal across members. check_pages verifies each against the rows (image via image_resolved, family from instance, ...).

equal_work.description: id of a check that proves every member computed the same thing (record counts, step count). A series whose work differs is not a scaling curve. 'none: <reason>' is allowed and surfaces as unproven.

attribution.description: patterns/cross-architecture.md's grades: same digest; same upstream version from another channel (aarchbio vs biocontainers, env twin); different versions (NGC 2023.2 on GPU vs conda-forge 2026.3 on CPU). Derivable in part from image_resolved; authored because the reason is not.

attribution_note.description: The confound in words: 'x86 runs the native Intel GKL pairHMM; arm64 the Java one'.

verdict.description: The author's reading, in patterns/sizing.md's vocabulary. The SPEED knee (`at`) is authored and confined to the series' rungs; no threshold rule derives one. The COST knee (lowest $/result rung) is derived. check_pages verifies only that the verdict is consistent with the rows: `at` is a rung, `through` is the top rung, a `wall` has a failed member above `at`.

shape.description: no-knee = speedup still ~linear at the top rung; knee = speed flattens at `at`; cost-climbs = speed rises, $/result rises; wall = rungs above `at` fail; answer-moves = output changes with the axis; flat = axis does not matter; monotonic = generation/size steps all in one direction; none = no reading.

at.description: Rung where the shape occurs (must be a member's axis value).

through.description: Highest rung tested. Must equal the members' max: 'no knee through 64' means untested beyond 64.

not_swept.description: An axis deliberately NOT measured, with the reason. Makes 'does X scale past N cores' answerable as 'not measured, because ...' instead of silence.

reason.description: As the README states it (salmon-real: 'quant finishes in about a minute against 43-78 s of fixed overhead').

claim.description: The README checks-table row's claim, verbatim.

kind.description: Which of CLAUDE.md's assertion shapes it is. 'reported' = printed, not asserted (bound '—'). 'offload' = the tool's log proves the accelerator path ran (GPU recipes' rank-count analogue).

observed.description: As printed in the README (string round-trip target).

outcome.description: One value for all chips, or per chip. 'fail' means asserted, failed, and left failing on purpose.

across_chips.description: identical = byte/digit-identical on every chip; fixed-point = agrees to a stated precision; path = differs by construction, never asserted equal across chips; last-bits = a direct, non-iterative computation that differs only in its last bits across builds, which nothing amplifies (neither a converged fixed point nor a path).

across_chips_evidence.description: The value pair or max diff that justifies across_chips. Required when across_chips is fixed-point, path or last-bits.

corename_sensitive.description: true if the value depends on OpenBLAS kernel selection (large blocked GEMM on a path).

cross_code.description: Authored once, in the measurement that runs the comparison; gen_catalog writes the reverse link into the counterpart.

with.description: measurements/<dir> or recipes/<name>, or 'published:<id>' for a published result (RELION, TMR).

tolerance_basis.description: Why the tolerance is the shared problem's precision, not the codes' observed agreement.

check.description: id of the check row that asserts it.

id.description: Globally unique; other records reference it by id rather than restating it.

symptom.description: The literal message or behaviour a reader sees, so they can find it by searching for it.

blames.description: What the symptom wrongly points at, if anything.

cost.description: Measured cost of hitting it, if known.

trap_refs.description: ids of traps owned by another record that also bit this one.

upstream.description: Issues this measurement filed, worked around, or is blocked by. State (open/closed) is NEVER stored: it is GitHub's.
